title: 2.7.5 Individual PA Part 5: Write the Steps
description: One problem, pick one of three, write the JavaScript it describes: a nested loop, a branch, a break or continue, a guard. One attempt, no Run button.

aiGrader.rubricTitle: Chapter 2 Individual PA, Part 5: Write the Steps
aiGrader.prompt:
The student submitted one JavaScript program answering one of three Part 5 problems (Seat Map, Word Grid, Fuel Log). Mark the CODE against the three criteria below. This is a summative, one-attempt item: mark what is on the paper, do not ask the student to run it.

The Chapter 2 ceiling: no functions, no arrays, no objects. Iteration only from loop counters and string indexing (word[i], word.length). A program that uses any of those loses the criterion that needed it and the feedback says which line crossed the ceiling.

Criterion 1 -- the branch (8 of the 20). An if / else if / else chain, with at least one compound condition using && or ||. Full credit: the chain resolves the problem's decision and the compound condition is meaningful, not (true && true). Partial: an if/else chain with a compound condition but no else-if rung, or a full chain where every condition is single. Withhold: no branch, or branches only.

Criterion 2 -- the loop and its nesting (9 of the 20). A loop inside a loop, both of which run. Full credit: two nested for/while forms, the inner one completing a full sweep per outer pass, with the bounds consistent with the problem's inputs. Partial credit ladder: 9 for a correct nest with an off-by-one in one bound; 6 for two loops that do not actually nest; 3 for one loop only where two are required. Withhold: no loop.

Criterion 3 -- loop control (3 of the 20, marked separately from criterion 2). At least one break or continue inside the loop that changes what would otherwise run: a continue past blocked seats or spaces, a break the moment the group size is met or the word ends. A control keyword sitting after the last statement of its loop body is decorative and earns nothing by itself.

Also check, without changing the 20: the header comment names Problem and Date (Partners is N/A on an individual paper); the limit is a const rather than a let; at least one template-literal console.log reports the result; typeof is reported for one value. Missing these are feedback lines, not point deductions -- the 20 points are the branch and the nested loop, and saying otherwise would re-weight the paper.

rubric.title: The branch: if / else if / else with && or ||
rubric.description: Full credit 8: a full chain resolving the problem's decision, at least one compound condition. Partial 5: chain present, conditions all simple. Partial 3: single if/else only. Withhold: no branch.

rubric.title: The nested loop, genuinely nested and genuinely running
rubric.description: Full credit 9: two nested loop forms that both execute, bounds consistent with the problem. Partial 6-7: off-by-one in a bound or the inner sweep does not complete. Partial 3: two loops that do not nest. Withhold: no loop.

rubric.title: break or continue that changes what runs
rubric.description: Full credit 3: a break or continue inside the nest that the problem's logic requires (skip blocked seats, stop at group size, break at word end). Partial 1: present but decorative. Withhold: none, or only switch-case breaks counted as loop control.
